nist-sp800-61r3.title: SP 800-61 Rev. 3: Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile
nist-sp800-61r3.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
nist-sp800-61r3.note: Published April 2025. Supersedes SP 800-61 Rev. 2 and organizes incident response around the six CSF 2.0 Functions.

nist-sp800-61r2.title: SP 800-61 Rev. 2: Computer Security Incident Handling Guide (withdrawn)
nist-sp800-61r2.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
nist-sp800-61r2.note: Source of the legacy four-phase lifecycle: Preparation; Detection & Analysis; Containment, Eradication & Recovery; Post-Incident Activity.

nist-csf2.title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29)
nist-csf2.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
nist-csf2.note: Six Functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover. Govern was added in 2.0.

cisa-stopransomware-guide.title: #StopRansomware Guide
cisa-stopransomware-guide.publisher: CISA, FBI, NSA and MS-ISAC (Joint Ransomware Task Force)
cisa-stopransomware-guide.note: Joint prevention and response checklist, updated October 2023. Recommends offline, encrypted, tested backups; MFA on remote access; isolating affected systems; and reporting to CISA or the FBI.

cisa-cpg.title: Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals (CPGs)
cisa-cpg.note: Baseline practices, including MFA, asset inventory, tested backups and an incident response plan. The #StopRansomware Guide maps its recommendations to these goals.

ofac-ransomware-advisory-2021.title: Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments
ofac-ransomware-advisory-2021.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
ofac-ransomware-advisory-2021.note: September 21, 2021. States that the U.S. government strongly discourages paying ransoms; sanctions violations can bring civil penalties on a strict-liability basis; prompt reporting to and cooperation with law enforcement are mitigating factors.

fbi-ic3-ransomware.title: Ransomware (IC3 crime information page)
fbi-ic3-ransomware.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
fbi-ic3-ransomware.note: The FBI does not support paying a ransom, since paying does not guarantee data recovery. It asks victims to report whether or not they pay.

fbi-ic3-2024-report.title: Internet Crime Report 2024
fbi-ic3-2024-report.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
fbi-ic3-2024-report.note: Press summaries report ransomware as the most-reported threat among critical-infrastructure complainants (about 1,400 complaints, up 9% from 2023). [VERIFY: confirm exact figures against the PDF before quoting on a slide.]

hhs-breach-notification-rule.title: Breach Notification Rule
hhs-breach-notification-rule.publisher: U.S. Department of Health & Human Services (HHS)
hhs-breach-notification-rule.note: Covered entities notify affected individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery. Breaches of 500+ individuals are also reported to HHS within 60 days.

ecfr-45-164-subpart-d.title: 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart D: Notification in the Case of Breach of Unsecured Protected Health Information (§§ 164.400–164.414)
ecfr-45-164-subpart-d.note: § 164.404 individual notice; § 164.406 media notice when more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction are affected; § 164.408 notice to the HHS Secretary.

hhs-ransomware-fact-sheet.title: Fact Sheet: Ransomware and HIPAA
hhs-ransomware-fact-sheet.note: When ransomware encrypts ePHI, a breach is presumed unless the entity can show a low probability that the PHI was compromised, based on a risk assessment.

hhs-change-healthcare-faq.title: Change Healthcare Cybersecurity Incident Frequently Asked Questions
hhs-change-healthcare-faq.note: A real-world parallel: OCR investigated the February 2024 ransomware attack on Change Healthcare, which disrupted claims and pharmacy processing nationwide. [VERIFY: press reports say a ransom was paid and the stolen data was still used for a second extortion attempt; confirm in a primary source such as congressional testimony before citing.]

tx-bcc-521-053.title: Texas Business & Commerce Code § 521.053: Notification Required Following Breach of Security of Computerized Data
tx-bcc-521-053.note: Notify affected individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after determining a breach occurred. If 250+ Texas residents are affected, notify the Texas Attorney General within 30 days, electronically (as amended effective Sept. 1, 2023).

tx-gov-2054-603.title: Texas Government Code § 2054.603: Security Incident Notification by State Agency or Local Government
tx-gov-2054-603.publisher: Texas Legislature / Texas Department of Information Resources (DIR)
tx-gov-2054-603.note: Local governments must report a security incident, including the introduction of ransomware, to DIR within 48 hours of discovery (moved here by SB 271, effective Sept. 1, 2023).

cisa-aa21-131a.title: AA21-131A: DarkSide Ransomware: Best Practices for Preventing Business Disruption from Ransomware Attacks
cisa-aa21-131a.note: Issued after the Colonial Pipeline incident. Recommends robust IT/OT segmentation, identifying IT/OT dependencies, developing and regularly testing manual controls, and keeping OT operating at needed capacity even if IT is compromised.

cisa-ot-primary-mitigations.title: Primary Mitigations to Reduce Cyber Threats to Operational Technology
cisa-ot-primary-mitigations.note: Includes removing OT connections to the public internet, segmenting IT and OT, and practising the ability to revert to manual operations. [VERIFY: publication date]

wws-ir-guide.title: Water and Wastewater Sector Incident Response Guide
wws-ir-guide.note: January 2024. Describes the federal support available to water utilities at each stage of the incident response lifecycle and how to request it.

cisa-water-vuln-scanning.title: CISA's Free Cyber Vulnerability Scanning for Water Utilities (fact sheet)
cisa-water-vuln-scanning.publisher: CISA, EPA, Water Sector Coordinating Council, ASDWA
cisa-water-vuln-scanning.note: A no-cost service that scans internet-facing systems and sends weekly reports with recommended fixes.

epa-cyberwater.title: Cybersecurity Planning for Water and Wastewater Utilities
epa-cyberwater.note: EPA resources, including the Cybersecurity Incident Action Checklist, an incident response plan template, and free cyber assessments for utilities.

fbi-psa-2019-high-impact.title: High-Impact Ransomware Attacks Threaten U.S. Businesses and Organizations (PSA I-100219-PSA)
fbi-psa-2019-high-impact.publisher: Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
fbi-psa-2019-high-impact.note: The FBI does not support paying a ransom, but recognizes that executives facing inoperability will evaluate all options. It urges victims to report regardless of whether they pay.
